question.prompt: Triangles \(ABC\) and \(ADC\) are isosceles with \(AB=BC\) and \(AD=DC.\) Point \(D\) is inside \(\triangle ABC,\) \(\angle ABC=40^\circ,\) and \(\angle ADC=140^\circ.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle BAD?\)

solutions.explanation:
Both isosceles triangles have base \(AC\), so each has equal angles at \(A\) and \(C\). Using the triangle angle sum gives
\[
\angle BAC=\frac{180^\circ-40^\circ}{2}=70^\circ
\]
and
\[
\angle DAC=\frac{180^\circ-140^\circ}{2}=20^\circ.
\]
Because \(D\) is inside \(\triangle ABC\), ray \(AD\) lies inside \(\angle BAC\). Therefore
\[
\angle BAD=70^\circ-20^\circ=50^\circ,
\]
choice D.
